'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Insurgency in the Maghreb (2002–present)|Insurgency in the Maghreb]]
**[[Mali War]]
*** [[Mopti bus massacre]]
****[[Militant]]s attack a bus carrying civilians in [[Mopti Region]], killing the driver, before [[Arson|setting it on fire]] and killing 31 passengers. The majority of the victims are women who were on their way to work at the local market. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-59528860 (BBC News)]
*[[Islamic State insurgency in Iraq (2017–present)|Islamic State insurgency in Iraq]]
**Seven [[Peshmerga]] fighters and three civilians are killed by [[Islamic State]] gunmen in a village in [[Makhmur, Iraq|Makhmour]], [[Erbil Governorate]], [[Kurdistan Region]], [[Iraq]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/12/3/several-civilians-and-peshmerga-killed-by-isil-in-iraq-makhmour (Al Jazeera)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Belgium]]
****Two [[hippo]]s at [[Antwerp Zoo]] test positive for [[COVID-19]] in [[Antwerp]], [[Belgium]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/hippos-with-runny-noses-test-positive-for-covid-19-at-belgian-zoo/a-60015051 (Deutsche Welle)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]]
****[[Germany]] surpasses six million cases of COVID-19. [https://www.urdupoint.com/en/world/number-of-confirmed-covid-19-cases-in-germany-1417280.html (Urdu Point)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland]]
****[[Taoiseach]] [[Micheál Martin]] announces that due to fears of the Omicron variant, from December 7 until January 9, nightclubs will be closed and restaurants and bars will only be allowed to offer table service for groups of no more than six people. Additionally, indoor services can only operate at 50% capacity and families can only have visitors from three other households. [https://news.sky.com/story/covid-19-ireland-brings-in-new-restrictions-ahead-of-christmas-due-to-very-stark-health-advice-12485681 (Sky News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Slovakia]]
****[[Slovakia]] reports a record 15,278 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 712,749. [https://apnews.com/article/coronavirus-pandemic-health-europe-slovakia-bratislava-8c5fc0ac3eea457532468b0afc8eb140 (AP)]
***[[Europe]] surpasses 75 million cases of COVID-19. [https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/europe-surpasses-75-million-covid-19-cases-amid-spread-omicron-2021-12-03/ (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[Malaysia]] reports its first case of the [[SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant]] in a 19-year-old student who travelled from South Africa on November 19 and is in [[quarantine]]. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/asia/malaysia-first-omicron-case-foreign-student-south-africa-singapore-2355891 (CNA)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Sri Lanka]]
****[[Sri Lanka]] reports its first case of the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant in an unvaccinated woman who travelled from [[Nigeria]]. [http://www.adaderana.lk/news/78887/sri-lanka-confirms-first-omicron-variant-case (Ada Derana)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico]]
***[[Mexico]] reports its first case of the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant in a 51-year-old man who travelled from South Africa. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/mexico-reports-first-case-of-omicron-covid-19-variant/2438156 (Anadolu Agency)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Africa]]
****[[South Africa]] surpasses three million cases of COVID-19. [https://www.cnn.com/2021/12/03/africa/south-africa-omicron-cases-surge-intl/index.html (CNN)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Tunisia]]
****[[Tunisia]] reports its first case of the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant in a [[People's Republic of the Congo|Congo]]lese man who travelled from [[Istanbul]]. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/1980291/middle-east (''Arab News'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[France–United Arab Emirates relations]]
**[[President of France|French president]] [[Emmanuel Macron]] meets [[United Arab Emirates|UAE]] [[crown prince]] [[Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan|Mohammed bin Zayed]] at [[Expo 2020]] in [[Dubai]]. The two men sign a major arms deal between the two nations. [https://www.thenationalnews.com/uae/government/2021/12/03/uae-and-france-sign-strategic-deals-as-emmanuel-macron-visits-expo/ (The National News)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2021 Oxford High School shooting]]
**The parents of Ethan Crumbley, James and Jennifer Crumbley, accused of [[terrorism in the United States|terrorism]] and [[murder (United States law)|murder]] in the shooting deaths and injuries at Ethan's school, are charged with [[manslaughter]] for their role in the incident. They are caught after fleeing the police. [https://www.cnn.com/us/live-news/oxford-school-shooting-michigan-12-03-21/h_c8293e66bd42f1922543bceb9beff015 (CNN)]
*[[Islam in Kosovo]]
**A [[Kosovo Albanian|Kosovar]] man is arrested for [[terrorism]] due to his ties to the [[Islamist]] [[al-Nusra Front]] in [[Syria]]. [https://thepublicsradio.org/article/kosovo-man-charged-with-joining-extremist-group-in-syria (The Public's Radio)]
*[[Law enforcement in Bosnia and Herzegovina|Police in Bosnia and Herzegovina]] arrest seven suspected [[war criminal]]s in [[Bijeljina]] and [[Sokolac, Bosnia and Herzegovina|Sokolac]] due to their reported [[massacre]] of 22 civilians during the [[Bosnian Genocide]]. [https://www.ctvnews.ca/world/bosnia-police-arrest-7-people-on-suspicion-of-war-crimes-1.5692097 (CTV News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Portugal|Portuguese]] [[Ministry of Internal Administration (Portugal)|Minister of Internal Administration]] [[Eduardo Cabrita]] resigns after a series of scandals, including an incident where his official car was involved in a [[car accident]] that killed a highway worker. [https://apnews.com/article/immigration-elections-migration-homicide-accidents-06ec67316d43a0b6fa36b71963123bb2 (AP)]

'''Sports'''
*[[Magnus Carlsen]] defeats challenger [[Ian Nepomniachtchi]] in [[Carlsen versus Nepomniachtchi, World Chess Championship 2021, Game 6|Game 6]] of the [[2021 World Chess Championship]] in a marathon 136 move game. It is the first decisive result in a regulation World Chess Championship game in more than 5 years and is also the longest game in World Chess Championship history. [https://www.theguardian.com/sport/live/2021/dec/03/magnus-carlsen-v-ian-nepomniachtchi-world-chess-championship-game-6-live (''The Guardian'')]
